---
title: "Generating derived quantities in Stan"
execute:

Once the sampler retains a joint draw $(\mu^{(s)},\sigma^{(s)})$, we often want
to do more than store those two numbers. We may want to express $\mu$ as a
duration ratio, generate a new passage contrast under the fitted model, or
record how much density the draw assigns to each observed passage. Stan's
[**generated quantities block**](https://mc-stan.org/docs/reference-manual/blocks.html)
performs these operations after each retained draw.

The timing is important. Code in this block cannot change which parameter
values the sampler visits because it runs after the draw has been produced.
It takes the paired values $(\mu^{(s)},\sigma^{(s)})$ as inputs and computes
additional outputs conditional on that pair.

For instance, suppose one retained draw has $\mu^{(s)}=.02$ and
$\sigma^{(s)}=.04$. The deterministic transformation
$\exp(\mu^{(s)})\approx1.020$ gives one duration-ratio draw. A call to
`student_t_rng(4, .02, .04)` adds new randomness and produces one replicated
passage contrast. A call to `student_t_lpdf(y[j] | 4, .02, .04)` adds no new
randomness; it evaluates the density of the observed $y_j$ under the same
parameter draw.

We will place these three operations beside one another and then inspect their
actual outputs. This will make clear which statements transform, simulate,
and evaluate.

## Three passage-level Student-t model outputs

The exact passage-level Student-t program contains

```stan
generated quantities {
  real geometric_duration_ratio = exp(mu);
  array[N] real y_rep;
  vector[N] log_lik;

  for (n in 1:N) {
    y_rep[n] = student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma);
    log_lik[n] = student_t_lpdf(y[n] | nu, mu, sigma);
  }
}
```

The transformed quantity is

$$
R=\exp(\mu).
$$

Within draw $s$, $r^{(s)}=\exp(\mu^{(s)})$. The input to $\mu$ consists of passage-level mean-log contrasts, so exponentiation produces a central geometric-scale noun-to-verb ratio for those passage summaries. A participant-level raw-duration ratio would require the unaggregated reader observations and a model for their variation.

For passage $j$, the replication and log-likelihood contribution are

$$
Y_j^{\mathrm{rep},(s)}
\sim t_4(\mu^{(s)},\sigma^{(s)}),
$$

$$
\ell_j^{(s)}
=
\log t_4(y_j\mid\mu^{(s)},\sigma^{(s)}).
$$

The `_rng` function simulates; the `_lpdf` function evaluates the observed response.

| Output type | Mathematics | Stan code | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| deterministic transform | $r^{(s)}=\exp(\mu^{(s)})$ | `exp(mu)` | one derived estimand for the same draw |
| posterior replication | $Y_j^{\mathrm{rep},(s)}\sim t_4(\mu^{(s)},\sigma^{(s)})$ | `student_t_rng(...)` | one new passage-level value under the fitted draw |
| pointwise log score | $\log p(y_j\mid\mu^{(s)},\sigma^{(s)})$ | `student_t_lpdf(...)` | density assigned to the observed passage value |

## Inspecting actual generated quantities

```{r}
#| label: summarize-provo-generated-quantities
library(posterior)

provo <- read.csv("data/provo/passage-summaries.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cache <- readRDS(
  "data/provo/provo-stan-draw-cache.rds"
)
draws <- as.data.frame(as_draws_df(cache$production_draws))
y_rep_names <- grep("^y_rep\\[", names(draws), value = TRUE)
log_lik_names <- grep("^log_lik\\[", names(draws), value = TRUE)
y_rep <- as.matrix(draws[, y_rep_names, drop = FALSE])
log_lik <- as.matrix(draws[, log_lik_names, drop = FALSE])

generated_summary <- data.frame(
  posterior_draws = nrow(draws),
  replicated_values_per_draw = ncol(y_rep),
  log_likelihood_values_per_draw = ncol(log_lik),
  mean_geometric_duration_ratio = mean(draws$geometric_duration_ratio),
  median_geometric_duration_ratio = median(draws$geometric_duration_ratio),
  mean_total_log_likelihood = mean(rowSums(log_lik))
)

stopifnot(nrow(provo) == 55L, ncol(y_rep) == 55L,
          ncol(log_lik) == 55L)
generated_summary
```

Every retained draw has one replicated value and one log-likelihood contribution for each of the 55 passages. Preserving this index is necessary for passage-level predictive checks and pointwise model-comparison calculations.

```{r}
#| label: plot-provo-generated-replicates
#| fig-cap: "Observed passage contrasts and one evenly spaced subset of complete posterior-replicated datasets."
library(ggplot2)
selected <- round(seq(1, nrow(y_rep), length.out = 40L))
replicate_means <- rowMeans(y_rep[selected, , drop = FALSE])
display <- rbind(
  data.frame(value = provo$noun_minus_verb_log_ffd, source = "observed passages"),
  data.frame(value = as.vector(y_rep[selected, , drop = FALSE]),
             source = "posterior replications")
)

histogram_opacity <- .45
ggplot(display, aes(value, fill = source)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 24,
                 position = "identity", alpha = histogram_opacity, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("observed passages" = "#8B1A1A",
                               "posterior replications" = "grey65")) +
  labs(x = "Passage noun-minus-verb mean log first fixation duration",
       y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Assignments in generated quantities cannot contribute to Stan's `target`. Moving a prior or likelihood there would remove it from inference. And grouping pointwise log likelihoods after fitting does not automatically change a passage-level prediction task into leave-one-reader-out evaluation; the aggregated passage table contains no reader rows to hold out.

## Recap and forward link

1. Generated quantities are evaluated conditionally on every retained joint posterior draw.
2. Deterministic transforms, replicated responses, and observed-data log scores answer different questions.
3. The passage index must be preserved for pointwise predictive work.
4. Generated quantities cannot repair or add a missing target-density term.

The [posterior predictive-check page](posterior-predictive-checks.qmd#replication-under-the-fitted-passage-level-student-t-model) compares the replicated passage data with the observations.

## Check your understanding

1. Which line simulates a replicated passage contrast?
2. Which line evaluates an observed contrast?
3. Why is $\exp(\mu)$ computed within every joint draw?
4. Can generated quantities repair a missing likelihood term?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. `y_rep[n] = student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma);` simulates a replicated passage contrast. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. `log_lik[n] = student_t_lpdf(y[n] | nu, mu, sigma);` evaluates the observed passage contrast. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Computing it within each draw preserves its joint uncertainty with all other parameters before the transformed quantity is summarized. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. No. Generated quantities run after sampling and cannot add a prior or likelihood contribution to `target`. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
